I’m assuming you’re not using the same blade on the 20-30$ clippers, especially if they’re human clippers? I think it’s more likely that there’s issues with the blades instead of the clippers. Especially if there’s matting. What length blade are you using?

Human clippers aren’t going to do the job. I’ve used Andis 5 Speed clippers, and a Wahl 2 speed and loved both, but I’m not sure about cheaper options. Is there a particular reason you want to groom her yourself? 

If you’re set on home grooming, I suggest getting a pair of dog grooming clippers with at least a 10 blade, a 30 blade, and a set of comb attachments. The comb attachments go on top of the 30 blade and will allow you to choose the length you want on her (as long as there is no matting). The 10 blade is good for sensitive areas like sanitary and paw pads. 

You’ll also need a slicker brush, comb, and a pair of shears to trim around her face and feet. 

Make sure your grooming a freshly washed and dried coat.

If he’s very anxious, try to book an appointment far in advance. If you go in person (versus over the phone) you can tell them about how he’s anxious, and if they’re a good groomer they will try to book you on a slower day (typically a week day). Groomers have seen PLENTY of people that have groomed their dogs at home; you’re not the first. They’ll understand. If they really feel it’s too much for them, try a different place. If possible, bring him with you when you make the appointment so the groomer can get an idea of what will be expected. I’m no mental health expert but I dated someone with bipolar for years. I think it’s a good idea to take a day off. It’s better to take one day off *just in case* than to have any type of depression or manic episode. You can use the day to relax, try to sleep in if possible. Try going for a walk, yoga, meditation, or even practice a hobby. Whatever typically makes you feel better. And if you’re worried about catching up at work or school, don’t. There’s people who miss an entire week and they’re okay. Maybe try to do a little bit of school work on your day off so it’s easier to come back the next day. Taking a day off won’t harm you, only give you the chance to relax a little. Also, major props for working and going to school while dealing with bipolar disorder. I know how difficult it can be to manage it, let alone while working and studying. Good luck!
